items.body_excerpt:
Expected Estimated +/- (EPM) is a player's predicted impact per 100 possessions as of today, using all career data before it.

Up = better defense
Right = better offense
Teal = positive impact
Magenta = negative impact

Learn more: dunksandthrees.com/about/epm

images.alt:
Scatter plot titled "NBA Player Impact Offense vs Defense," showing Estimated Plus-Minus (EPM) for the 2026-27 season as of Nov. 13, 2026. EPM is each player's predicted contribution in points per 100 possessions, based on his whole career. Offense runs left to right and defense runs bottom to top. Teal dots are players with a positive overall EPM and pink dots are players with a negative one. Bigger dots mean more minutes per game. Diagonal dashed lines mark overall EPM levels of -10, -5, 0, +5 and +10.

Most players sit in a cloud near the middle. Victor Wembanyama stands out by himself in the top right, at about +5.4 on offense and +5.4 on defense, which puts him just past the +10 line. Luka Doncic, Stephen Curry and SGA are farthest to the right, at about +8 on offense, but each is only around +1 on defense. Nikola Jokic, Kawhi Leonard, Tyrese Haliburton and LaMelo Ball are close behind on offense. LaMelo is the only one of them sitting just below zero on defense.

Rudy Gobert and Ausar Thompson are the top defenders, at nearly +5, but both are slightly negative on offense. Alex Caruso is right next to them, at about even on offense. Chet Holmgren, Jarrett Allen, Karl-Anthony Towns, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Jayson Tatum all land in the positive-positive quadrant. Jaylen Brown sits almost exactly at zero on offense and a little above zero on defense.

AJ Johnson, Jahmai Mashack and Bronny James are alone in the far bottom left, at around -6 on offense and -3 on defense.

Data from DunksAndThrees.com. Viz by @Hoopinformatics.com on Bluesky.
